---
title: "Merged entries, per index"
indexes:
  - name: plants
    title: Index of Plants
  - name: places
    title: Index of Places
filters:
  - index
---

A term marked in different ways is printed as one entry, and the LaTeX
back-end reports each entry it merged. This document declares two indexes, so
each report also names the index the entry is in. The first index holds one
term for each of the four merged shapes. A fifth term is marked in both
indexes, plainly in one and with a cross-reference in the other, so neither
index merges anything for it and neither reports it.

## The four merged shapes

A plain mark beside one cross-reference: [Alder]{.index index="plants"} and
[Alder]{.index index="plants" see="Birch"}.

A plain mark beside two different cross-references:
[Cedar]{.index index="plants"}, [Cedar]{.index index="plants" see="Elm"} and
[Cedar]{.index index="plants" see="Fir"}.

Two different cross-references and no plain mark:
[Hazel]{.index index="plants" see="Larch"} and
[Hazel]{.index index="plants" see="Maple"}.

Three different cross-references and no plain mark:
[Oak]{.index index="plants" see="Pine"},
[Oak]{.index index="plants" see="Rowan"} and
[Oak]{.index index="plants" see="Spruce"}.

## One term in both indexes

A plain mark in the first index, [Willow]{.index index="plants"}, and a
cross-reference in the second, [Willow]{.index index="places" see="Yukon"}.

## The targets

Every target above is a term of its own, marked in the index its
cross-reference is in: [Birch]{.index index="plants"},
[Elm]{.index index="plants"}, [Fir]{.index index="plants"},
[Larch]{.index index="plants"}, [Maple]{.index index="plants"},
[Pine]{.index index="plants"}, [Rowan]{.index index="plants"},
[Spruce]{.index index="plants"} and [Yukon]{.index index="places"}.
